text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Deputy Prime Minister Jozef Kalman said on Thursday Slovakia hoped Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl would meet by the end of the year.
- Slovakia will reform its tax system within some four to five years, with the main focus being changes to income and property tax, Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said.

- Troubled engineering company Podpolianske Strojarne Detva a.s. said it would have to layoff half of its 2,600 employees if it did not find sources for some 150 million crowns neccessary to complete its contracts.
- All major opposition parties have repeatedly said they would not hold talks with Premier Meciar and his ruling coalition until Intrerior Minister Gustav Krajci is dismissed.

- Slovak commercial banks agreed to settle previously agreed Forward Rate Agreements (FRA) according to the latest quoted Bratislava Interbank Offered Rate (BRIBOR) on May 28. The BRIBOR has not been quoted over the past three weeks due to an accute liquidity shortage on the interbank market which has paralysed trading activity.
SME - Minister Krajci on Thursday survived a non-confidence vote in the parliament as ruling coalition deputies boycotted the vote on his dismissal proposed by the opposition.
- Parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic has called another extraordinary session for Krajci's dismissal on Friday.
- Krajci has repeatedly rejected accusations of thwarting referendums on NATO membership and presidential elections and said he would resign his post only if President Michal Kovac resigns.
- Opposition Democratic Union (DU) said it would support initiating early elections if the entire opposition agrees on such a move.
PRAVDA - National Property Fund President (NPF), Stefan Gavornik, said the NPF presidium has not so far discussed any project for privatising the two largest commercial banks, VUB and IRB.

- Opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) said the law on so-called revitalisation of troubled state companies, currently being discussed in parliament, was in contradiction with free market principles and would boost corruption.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovak banks are expected not to meet their minimum reserves requirements in the first half of the month since the central bank continues keeping the market short of crown liquidity to prevent pressure on the currency.
- Slovak industrial production rose by 9.0 percent year- on-year in April.
- The Slovak capital, Bratislava, posted a 36.5 million budget deficit in 1996, on revenues totalling 1.803 billion crowns and expenditures at 1.838 billion crowns.
